 43: \noindent\textbf{Mathematics Subject Classification (2020).}
 44: 11B39, 11A07, 11A25.
  1: \section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}
  2: %% ====================================================================
  3: 
  4: For an integer $q\ge1$, the \emph{rank of apparition} (or \emph{order of
  5: appearance}) $\alpha(q)$ is the least positive index $r$ such that $q\mid
  6: F_r$, where $F_0=0$ and $F_1=1$.  The existence of this index is recalled in
  7: Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-rank}.  We use the conventions $\alpha(1)=1$ and
  8: $D_1=\operatorname{Div}(F_1)=\{1\}$.  For $n\ge2$, write
  9: \[
 10:  D_n:=\operatorname{Div}(F_n),\qquad
 11:  B_n:=\{q\in D_n:\alpha(q)=n\},\qquad
 12:  \mathcal M_n:=\min_{\mid} B_n .
 13: \]
 14: Thus $B_n$ is the set of moduli that first divide a Fibonacci number at
 15: index $n$, and $\mathcal M_n$ is its set of divisibility-minimal elements.
 16: The boundary layer is empty: $B_2=\mathcal M_2=\varnothing$.  Throughout,
 17: $\log$ is natural, $\mathcal P(n)$ is the set of prime divisors of $n$,
 18: $\omega(n)=\#\mathcal P(n)$, and $\Omega(n)$ counts prime factors with
 19: multiplicity.
 20: 
 21: \subsection*{Prior work and novelty boundary}
 22: 
 23: The cardinality of $B_n$ is contained in Stroi\'nski's general
 24: $\alpha$-contraction formalism \cite{Stroinski2016AlphaContraction}; classical
 25: M\"obius identities for Fibonacci divisibility appear in
 26: \cite{Halton1966DivisibilityFibonacci,FultonMorris1969ArithmeticalFunctions}.
 27: For primes, the nearest prior distribution results are due to Kiss.  His 1988
 28: work treats primitive divisors and accumulated primitive parts
 29: \cite{Kiss1988PrimitiveDivisors}, while his paper on ranks of apparition of
 30: primes in Lucas sequences bounds averages of $\alpha(p)/p$
 31: \cite{Kiss1989RankApparition}.  These results, and Stroi\'nski's cumulative
 32: bound for primes with bounded rank, do not give upper-distribution estimates
 33: for the growing exact fibers
 34: \[
 35:  \Pi_\alpha(d):=\{p\text{ prime}:\alpha(p)=d\},\qquad
 36:  a(d):=\#\Pi_\alpha(d).
 37: \]
 38: The distinction between cumulative rank estimates and the individual
 39: multiplicities $a(d)$ is decisive below.
 40: 
 41: Other nearby work studies different aspects of the order-of-appearance map.
 42: Luca and Pomerance study its local behavior under additive shifts
 43: \cite{LucaPomerance2014LocalBehavior}; Trojovsk\'a and
 44: FitzGibbons--Javaheri--Miller--Verga study periodic points and dynamics
 45: \cite{Trojovska2020PeriodicPoints,
 46: FitzGibbonsJavaheriMillerVerga2025Dynamics}; and Sanna gives distribution
 47: theorems for rank divisibility and, under GRH, fixed indices of appearance
 48: \cite{Sanna2022RankDivisibility,Sanna2024IndexAppearance}.  Rank divisibility
 49: $d\mid\alpha(p)$ does not isolate $\alpha(p)=d$, and the fixed-index theorem
 50: does not provide the growing exact-fiber uniformity required here.
 51: 
 52: The structural starting points of this paper are classical:
 53: \[
 54:  q\mid F_m\Longleftrightarrow\alpha(q)\mid m,\qquad
 55:  \gcd(F_r,F_s)=F_{\gcd(r,s)},
 56: \]
 57: and
 58: \[
 59:  \alpha(\operatorname{lcm}(u,v))
 60:  =\operatorname{lcm}(\alpha(u),\alpha(v)).
 61: \]
 62: See \cite{Wall1960FibonacciModm,Vinson1963RankApparition}; Renault proves the
 63: last identity for the more general $(a,b)$-Fibonacci sequence
 64: \cite{Renault2013PeriodRankOrder}.  Exact-rank prime existence is supplied by
 65: Carmichael and Bilu--Hanrot--Voutier
 66: \cite{Carmichael1913PrimitiveDivisors,
 67: BiluHanrotVoutier2001PrimitiveDivisorsLucas}.  The upper-set identity,
 68: coordinatewise lcm test, prime-power lifting formulas, and private-coordinate
 69: injection are consequences of these inputs.  We record them as lemmas and do
 70: not claim them as independent arithmetic advances.
 71: 
 72: \subsection*{The reduction to a weighted arithmetic problem}
 73: 
 74: For a prime power $\theta=p^e$, call $\theta$ atomic when lowering it to
 75: $p^{e-1}$ lowers its rank.  Relative to $n$, its rank has a full-coordinate
 76: support $T_n(\theta)$ and an essential support $E_n(\theta)$, the coordinates
 77: lost on lowering.  An $n$-witness cover is a pairwise coprime collection of
 78: atoms whose full supports cover $\mathcal P(n)$ and in which each atom has an
 79: essential coordinate absent from all other full supports.
 80: 
 81: \begin{previewtheorem}[Witness-cover classification]
 82: Multiplication is a bijection from $n$-witness covers to $\mathcal M_n$.
 83: Consequently every $m\in\mathcal M_n$ has a unique atomic factorization and
 84: \[
 85:  \omega(m)\le\omega(n).
 86: \]
 87: \end{previewtheorem}
 88: 
 89: This is Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification}.  The classification turns the
 90: counting problem into a minimal-cover problem, but it does not erase the
 91: number of primes available at each exact rank.  The following result gives a
 92: necessary weighted obstruction on a positive-density family.
 93: 
 94: \begin{previewtheorem}[Weighted odd-layer obstruction]
 95: Let $n\ge3$ be odd, set $V=\mathcal P(n)$, and for
 96: $\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V$ put
 97: $n_S=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell^{\nu_\ell(n)}$.  If
 98: $\operatorname{MinCov}(V)$ denotes the irredundant covers of $V$ by nonempty
 99: subsets, then
100: \[
101:  \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
102:  \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S)
103:  \le\#\mathcal M_n.
104: \]
105: \end{previewtheorem}
106: 
107: The general rank-pure embedding is
108: Theorem~\ref{thm:rank-pure-universality}, and the displayed obstruction is
109: Corollary~\ref{cor:odd-weighted-cover-obstruction}.  The sum is the exact
110: cardinality of an explicit rank-pure sector, so any upper equivalent for
111: $\#\mathcal M_n$ must control it.  It need not exhaust the full fiber:
112: $\alpha(13)=7$ and $\alpha(13^2)=91$, so the odd squarefree layer $91$ already
113: has the ladder generator $169$ outside the rank-pure sector.
114: 
115: Let $C_k$ be the number of irredundant covers of a labelled $k$-set.
116: Hearne--Wagner give its exact enumeration
117: \cite{HearneWagner1973MinimalCovers}, and the split-graph asymptotics of
118: Bender--Richmond--Wormald and Troyka imply
119: \[
120:  \log C_k=\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+O(k)
121: \]
122: \cite{BenderRichmondWormald1985ChordalSplit,Troyka2019SplitGraphs}.  For odd
123: $n$, define the normalized weighted excess
124: \[
125:  \mathcal W(n):=\frac1{C_{\omega(n)}}
126:  \sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(\mathcal P(n))}
127:  \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}a(n_S).
128: \]
129: Then the rank-pure sector satisfies
130: \begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-weighted-lower-bound}
131:  \log\#\mathcal M_n
132:  \ge\frac{\log2}{4}\omega(n)^2+\log\mathcal W(n)+O(\omega(n)).
133: \end{equation}
134: 
135: Since odd integers have positive density and
136: $\omega(n)\sim\log\log n$ for almost all of them, the proposed tier-up theorem
137: \begin{equation}\label{eq:target-normal-order}
138:  \log\#\mathcal M_n\sim
139:  \frac{\log2}{4}(\log\log n)^2
140:  \qquad\text{for almost all }n
141: \end{equation}
142: requires
143: \[
144:  \log\mathcal W(n)=o((\log\log n)^2)
145: \]
146: outside an $o(x)$ exceptional set of odd $n\le x$.  No result
147: located in the arXiv, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, or zbMATH searches proves
148: this weighted exact-rank dispersion estimate.  The available primitive-divisor
149: theorems give existence, while the nearest distribution theorems control
150: cumulative ranks, rank divisibility, the size of one primitive divisor, or a
151: fixed index of appearance.  None controls the simultaneous weights
152: $a(n_S)$ over the divisor family of a typical $n$.
153: 
154: \subsection*{Unconditional bounds and the failed step}
155: 
156: For a general $n$, let $R(n)$ be the largest number of atomic prime powers
157: having one fixed essential/full support pair.  Private-coordinate encoding and
158: the rank-pure construction give, for $k=\omega(n)\ge3$,
159: \[
160:  (2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}-1)^{\lceil k/2\rceil}
161:  \le\#\mathcal M_n
162:  \le\sum_{s=1}^k\binom{k}{s}(2R(n))^s2^{s(k-s)}.
163: \]
164: Hence
165: \begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-entropy-bounds}
166:  \frac{\log2}{4}k^2-O(1)
167:  \le\log\#\mathcal M_n
168:  \le\frac{\log2}{4}k^2+k\log R(n)+O(k).
169: \end{equation}
170: The lower estimate already gives the target constant after the
171: Hardy--Ramanujan normal-order theorem.  The upper estimate proves
172: \eqref{eq:target-normal-order} if $\log R(n)=o(\omega(n))$ almost everywhere,
173: but that maximum condition is only sufficient.  The weighted-cover condition

186: \]

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify the squarefree exact-fiber converse and weighted-cover sharpness."""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, Tuple
+
+from verify_deepening_delta import (
+    alpha_for_fn_divisor,
+    factorint,
+    factorint_fibonacci,
+    upper_fiber_threshold,
+)
+
+
+Subset = FrozenSet[int]
+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]
+
+
+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)
+        )
+        if frozenset().union(*cover) != vertex_set:
+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)
+
+
+def weighted_cover_partition(size: int, weights: Dict[Subset, int]) -> int:
+    """Return the weighted partition function over irredundant covers."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    if set(weights) != set(subsets) or any(weights[subset] < 1 for subset in subsets):
+        raise ValueError("weights must be positive on every nonempty subset")
+    return sum(
+        _product(weights[edge] for edge in cover)
+        for cover in minimal_covers(size)
+    )
+
+
+def _product(values: Iterable[int]) -> int:
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def sharp_mass_lower_bound(size: int, total_mass: int) -> int:
+    """Return C_k + total_mass - (2^k - 1)."""
+    baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    return len(minimal_covers(size)) + total_mass - baseline_mass
+
+
+def extremal_full_support_profile(size: int, total_mass: int) -> Dict[Subset, int]:
+    """Concentrate all mass above one on the full support."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+    weights[frozenset(range(size))] += total_mass - baseline_mass
+    return weights
+
+
+def squarefree_minimal_generators(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the squarefree elements among the verified minimal generators."""
+    result = upper_fiber_threshold(n)
+    return tuple(
+        value
+        for value in result.minimal_generators
+        if all(exponent == 1 for exponent in factorint(value).values())
+    )
+
+
+def _exact_rank_primes(n: int) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    primes_by_rank: Dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for prime, _ in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime, n)
+        primes_by_rank.setdefault(rank, []).append(prime)
+    return {
+        rank: tuple(sorted(primes))
+        for rank, primes in primes_by_rank.items()
+    }
+
+
+def rank_pure_products(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Construct the rank-pure products directly from exact-rank prime covers."""
+    n_factors = factorint(n)
+    if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in n_factors.values()):
+        raise ValueError("rank-pure converse verifier requires squarefree n")
+    coordinates = tuple(sorted(n_factors))
+    primes_by_rank = _exact_rank_primes(n)
+    products = set()
+    for cover in minimal_covers(len(coordinates)):
+        ranks = tuple(
+            _product(coordinates[index] for index in support)
+            for support in cover
+        )
+        choices = []
+        fillable = True
+        for rank in ranks:
+            primes = primes_by_rank.get(rank, tuple())
+            if not primes:
+                fillable = False
+                break
+            choices.append(primes)
+        if not fillable:
+            continue
+        for selected in itertools.product(*choices):
+            products.add(_product(selected))
+    return tuple(sorted(products))
+
+
+def run_battery(max_index: int) -> str:
+    """Run exhaustive combinatorial checks and squarefree Fibonacci comparisons."""
+    if max_index < 30:
+        raise ValueError("max_index must be at least 30")
+    profile_checks = 0
+    for size in range(1, 5):
+        baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+        for excess in range(9):
+            total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+            profile = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+            actual = weighted_cover_partition(size, profile)
+            expected = sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass)
+            if actual != expected:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"sharp profile failed for size={size}, mass={total_mass}"
+                )
+            profile_checks += 1
+
+    checked_indices = []
+    checked_elements = 0
+    for n in range(3, max_index + 1):
+        if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in factorint(n).values()):
+            continue
+        expected = squarefree_minimal_generators(n)
+        actual = rank_pure_products(n)
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"squarefree slice failed at n={n}: {actual} != {expected}"
+            )
+        checked_indices.append(n)
+        checked_elements += len(actual)
+
+    lines = [
+        "Squarefree-fiber and weighted-cover verification",
+        "=================================================",
+        "Weighted minimal-cover equality profiles: sizes 1 <= k <= 4,",
+        "  excess masses 0 <= E <= 8",
+        f"  exact equality checks = {profile_checks}",
+        f"Squarefree Fibonacci indices: 3 <= n <= {max_index}",
+        f"  indices checked = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  rank-pure/squarefree set equalities = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  squarefree minimal generators compared = {checked_elements}",
+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-index", type=int, default=210)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("artifacts/squarefree_slice_verification.txt"),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run_battery(args.max_index)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="ascii")
+    print(report, end="")
+    print(f"Saved report: {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+The rank-pure sector has a canonical description on squarefree indices.  In
+particular, it is not then an auxiliary class defined only through the cover
+construction.

+\begin{corollary}[Canonical squarefree exact-fiber slice]
+\label{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+Let $n\ge3$ be squarefree.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+ \mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}
+ =\mathcal M_n\cap\{q:\mu^2(q)=1\}
+ =\min_{\mid}\{q:\alpha(q)=n,\ \mu^2(q)=1\}.
+\end{equation}
+Thus the weighted sum in
+\eqref{eq:rank-pure-weighted-sector} counts exactly the divisibility-minimal
+squarefree elements of the standard exact fiber $\alpha^{-1}(n)$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
+$B_n=\{q:\alpha(q)=n\}=\alpha^{-1}(n)$.  If a squarefree member of $B_n$
+has a proper divisor in $B_n$, that divisor is again squarefree.  Hence
+minimality in the squarefree part of the exact fiber is equivalent to
+membership in $\mathcal M_n$.
+
+Every element of $\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$ is a product of distinct primes and
+belongs to $\mathcal M_n$, which proves one inclusion in the first equality.
+Conversely, let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ be squarefree.  Its unique atomic
+factorization from Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} consists only of
+prime atoms $p$.  Put $S=T_n(p)$.  Since $\alpha(p)\mid n$ and $n$ is
+squarefree,
+\[
+ \alpha(p)=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell=n_S.
+\]
+Moreover $d^-(p)=1$, so $E_n(p)=T_n(p)=S$.  The witness-cover conditions are
+therefore precisely that the distinct supports $S$ form an irredundant cover
+of $\mathcal P(n)$.  No such support lies in $\mathcal E_n$, because the
+corresponding prime $p$ itself has exact rank $n_S$.  Thus the atomic
+factorization of $m$ is one of the uniquely represented products defining
+$\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$.  This proves the reverse inclusion and the result.
+\end{proof}

+The following sharp extremal calculation separates total primitive-prime
+mass from the dispersion information retained by the cover polynomial.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
+$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
+\[
+ Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+
+Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\ge
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
+extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
+asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
+over all minimal covers therefore gives
+\[
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
+ =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\]
+The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
+full-support profile has weighted sum
+$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
+to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of

+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
+ =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
+Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

\subsection*{Organization}

Section~\ref{sec:prelim} records the classical rank and primitive-divisor
inputs.  Section~\ref{sec:upper-fibers} proves the witness-cover
classification.  Section~\ref{sec:growth} develops the rank-window,
fibotomic, weighted rank-pure, and support-entropy estimates.  The final
section states the remaining arithmetic interfaces.  The supplement contains
the connected-block factorization, exact support spectra, complete
classifications for $\omega(n)\le3$, secondary asymptotics, and reproducible
finite computations.  Keeping those structural consequences separate leaves
the article centered on the arithmetic obstruction exposed by
\eqref{eq:intro-weighted-lower-bound}.

+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]
+
+
+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)
+        )
+        if frozenset().union(*cover) != vertex_set:
+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)
+
+
+def weighted_cover_partition(size: int, weights: Dict[Subset, int]) -> int:
+    """Return the weighted partition function over irredundant covers."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    if set(weights) != set(subsets) or any(weights[subset] < 1 for subset in subsets):
+        raise ValueError("weights must be positive on every nonempty subset")
+    return sum(
+        _product(weights[edge] for edge in cover)
+        for cover in minimal_covers(size)
+    )
+
+
+def _product(values: Iterable[int]) -> int:
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def sharp_mass_lower_bound(size: int, total_mass: int) -> int:
+    """Return C_k + total_mass - (2^k - 1)."""
+    baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    return len(minimal_covers(size)) + total_mass - baseline_mass
+
+
+def extremal_full_support_profile(size: int, total_mass: int) -> Dict[Subset, int]:
+    """Concentrate all mass above one on the full support."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+    weights[frozenset(range(size))] += total_mass - baseline_mass
+    return weights
+
+
+def squarefree_minimal_generators(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the squarefree elements among the verified minimal generators."""
+    result = upper_fiber_threshold(n)
+    return tuple(
+        value
+        for value in result.minimal_generators
+        if all(exponent == 1 for exponent in factorint(value).values())
+    )
+
+
+def _exact_rank_primes(n: int) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    primes_by_rank: Dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for prime, _ in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime, n)
+        primes_by_rank.setdefault(rank, []).append(prime)
+    return {
+        rank: tuple(sorted(primes))
+        for rank, primes in primes_by_rank.items()
+    }
+
+
+def rank_pure_products(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Construct the rank-pure products directly from exact-rank prime covers."""
+    n_factors = factorint(n)
+    if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in n_factors.values()):
+        raise ValueError("rank-pure converse verifier requires squarefree n")
+    coordinates = tuple(sorted(n_factors))
+    primes_by_rank = _exact_rank_primes(n)
+    products = set()
+    for cover in minimal_covers(len(coordinates)):
+        ranks = tuple(
+            _product(coordinates[index] for index in support)
+            for support in cover
+        )
+        choices = []
+        fillable = True
+        for rank in ranks:
+            primes = primes_by_rank.get(rank, tuple())
+            if not primes:
+                fillable = False
+                break
+            choices.append(primes)
+        if not fillable:
+            continue
+        for selected in itertools.product(*choices):
+            products.add(_product(selected))
+    return tuple(sorted(products))
+
+
+def run_battery(max_index: int) -> str:
+    """Run exhaustive combinatorial checks and squarefree Fibonacci comparisons."""
+    if max_index < 30:
+        raise ValueError("max_index must be at least 30")
+    profile_checks = 0
+    for size in range(1, 5):
+        baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+        for excess in range(9):
+            total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+            profile = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+            actual = weighted_cover_partition(size, profile)
+            expected = sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass)
+            if actual != expected:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"sharp profile failed for size={size}, mass={total_mass}"
+                )
+            profile_checks += 1
+
+    checked_indices = []
+    checked_elements = 0
+    for n in range(3, max_index + 1):
+        if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in factorint(n).values()):
+            continue
+        expected = squarefree_minimal_generators(n)
+        actual = rank_pure_products(n)
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"squarefree slice failed at n={n}: {actual} != {expected}"
+            )
+        checked_indices.append(n)
+        checked_elements += len(actual)
+
+    lines = [
+        "Squarefree-fiber and weighted-cover verification",
+        "=================================================",
+        "Weighted minimal-cover equality profiles: sizes 1 <= k <= 4,",
+        "  excess masses 0 <= E <= 8",
+        f"  exact equality checks = {profile_checks}",
+        f"Squarefree Fibonacci indices: 3 <= n <= {max_index}",
+        f"  indices checked = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  rank-pure/squarefree set equalities = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  squarefree minimal generators compared = {checked_elements}",
+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-index", type=int, default=210)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("artifacts/squarefree_slice_verification.txt"),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run_battery(args.max_index)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="ascii")
+    print(report, end="")
+    print(f"Saved report: {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+The rank-pure sector has a canonical description on squarefree indices.  In
+particular, it is not then an auxiliary class defined only through the cover
+construction.
+
+\begin{corollary}[Canonical squarefree exact-fiber slice]
+\label{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+Let $n\ge3$ be squarefree.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+ \mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}
+ =\mathcal M_n\cap\{q:\mu^2(q)=1\}
+ =\min_{\mid}\{q:\alpha(q)=n,\ \mu^2(q)=1\}.
+\end{equation}
+Thus the weighted sum in
+\eqref{eq:rank-pure-weighted-sector} counts exactly the divisibility-minimal
+squarefree elements of the standard exact fiber $\alpha^{-1}(n)$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
+$B_n=\{q:\alpha(q)=n\}=\alpha^{-1}(n)$.  If a squarefree member of $B_n$
+has a proper divisor in $B_n$, that divisor is again squarefree.  Hence
+minimality in the squarefree part of the exact fiber is equivalent to
+membership in $\mathcal M_n$.
+
+Every element of $\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$ is a product of distinct primes and
+belongs to $\mathcal M_n$, which proves one inclusion in the first equality.
+Conversely, let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ be squarefree.  Its unique atomic
+factorization from Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} consists only of
+prime atoms $p$.  Put $S=T_n(p)$.  Since $\alpha(p)\mid n$ and $n$ is
+squarefree,
+\[
+ \alpha(p)=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell=n_S.
+\]
+Moreover $d^-(p)=1$, so $E_n(p)=T_n(p)=S$.  The witness-cover conditions are
+therefore precisely that the distinct supports $S$ form an irredundant cover
+of $\mathcal P(n)$.  No such support lies in $\mathcal E_n$, because the
+corresponding prime $p$ itself has exact rank $n_S$.  Thus the atomic
+factorization of $m$ is one of the uniquely represented products defining
+$\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$.  This proves the reverse inclusion and the result.
+\end{proof}
+

+The following sharp extremal calculation separates total primitive-prime
+mass from the dispersion information retained by the cover polynomial.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
+$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
+\[
+ Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+
+Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\ge
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
+extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
+asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
+over all minimal covers therefore gives
+\[
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
+ =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\]
+The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
+full-support profile has weighted sum
+$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
+to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of
+$F_n$, and $a(1)=0$, so
+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
+ =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
+Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regression tests for the squarefree-fiber and sharpness verifier."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+from verify_squarefree_slice import (
+    extremal_full_support_profile,
+    minimal_covers,
+    rank_pure_products,
+    sharp_mass_lower_bound,
+    squarefree_minimal_generators,
+    weighted_cover_partition,
+)
+
+
+class SquarefreeSliceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_nonempty_subset_occurs_in_a_minimal_cover(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+            covers = minimal_covers(size)
+            for subset_size in range(1, size + 1):
+                for subset in itertools.combinations(vertex_set, subset_size):
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        any(frozenset(subset) in cover for cover in covers)
+                    )
+
+    def test_sharp_mass_bound_for_small_integer_profiles(self):
+        for size in range(1, 4):
+            subsets = tuple(
+                subset
+                for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+                for subset in map(frozenset, itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size))
+            )
+            baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+            for excess_locations in itertools.product(range(len(subsets)), repeat=3):
+                weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+                for location in excess_locations:
+                    weights[subsets[location]] += 1
+                partition = weighted_cover_partition(size, weights)
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(
+                    partition,
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, baseline_mass + 3),
+                )
+
+    def test_full_support_profile_attains_the_bound(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+            for excess in (0, 1, 5, 17):
+                total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+                weights = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    weighted_cover_partition(size, weights),
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass),
+                )
+
+    def test_rank_pure_products_equal_squarefree_minima(self):
+        squarefree_indices = (
+            3,
+            5,
+            6,
+            7,
+            10,
+            15,
+            21,
+            30,
+            35,
+            42,
+            55,
+            66,
+            70,
+            78,
+            105,
+        )
+        for n in squarefree_indices:
+            with self.subTest(n=n):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    rank_pure_products(n),
+                    squarefree_minimal_generators(n),
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

+"""Verify the squarefree exact-fiber converse and weighted-cover sharpness."""
+

+Subset = FrozenSet[int]
+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]

+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)

+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)

+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]

+
+\begin{corollary}[Canonical squarefree exact-fiber slice]
+\label{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+Let $n\ge3$ be squarefree.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+ \mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}
+ =\mathcal M_n\cap\{q:\mu^2(q)=1\}
+ =\min_{\mid}\{q:\alpha(q)=n,\ \mu^2(q)=1\}.
+\end{equation}
+Thus the weighted sum in
+\eqref{eq:rank-pure-weighted-sector} counts exactly the divisibility-minimal
+squarefree elements of the standard exact fiber $\alpha^{-1}(n)$.
+\end{corollary}

+\begin{proof}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
+$B_n=\{q:\alpha(q)=n\}=\alpha^{-1}(n)$.  If a squarefree member of $B_n$
+has a proper divisor in $B_n$, that divisor is again squarefree.  Hence
+minimality in the squarefree part of the exact fiber is equivalent to
+membership in $\mathcal M_n$.
+
+Every element of $\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$ is a product of distinct primes and
+belongs to $\mathcal M_n$, which proves one inclusion in the first equality.
+Conversely, let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ be squarefree.  Its unique atomic
+factorization from Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} consists only of
+prime atoms $p$.  Put $S=T_n(p)$.  Since $\alpha(p)\mid n$ and $n$ is
+squarefree,
+\[
+ \alpha(p)=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell=n_S.
+\]
+Moreover $d^-(p)=1$, so $E_n(p)=T_n(p)=S$.  The witness-cover conditions are
+therefore precisely that the distinct supports $S$ form an irredundant cover
+of $\mathcal P(n)$.  No such support lies in $\mathcal E_n$, because the
+corresponding prime $p$ itself has exact rank $n_S$.  Thus the atomic
+factorization of $m$ is one of the uniquely represented products defining
+$\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$.  This proves the reverse inclusion and the result.
+\end{proof}
+

+The following sharp extremal calculation separates total primitive-prime
+mass from the dispersion information retained by the cover polynomial.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
+$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
+\[
+ Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+
+Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\ge
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
+extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
+asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
+over all minimal covers therefore gives
+\[
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
+ =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\]
+The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
+full-support profile has weighted sum
+$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
+to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of
+$F_n$, and $a(1)=0$, so
+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
+ =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
+Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regression tests for the squarefree-fiber and sharpness verifier."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+from verify_squarefree_slice import (
+    extremal_full_support_profile,
+    minimal_covers,
+    rank_pure_products,
+    sharp_mass_lower_bound,
+    squarefree_minimal_generators,
+    weighted_cover_partition,
+)
+
+
+class SquarefreeSliceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_nonempty_subset_occurs_in_a_minimal_cover(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+            covers = minimal_covers(size)
+            for subset_size in range(1, size + 1):
+                for subset in itertools.combinations(vertex_set, subset_size):
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        any(frozenset(subset) in cover for cover in covers)
+                    )
+
+    def test_sharp_mass_bound_for_small_integer_profiles(self):
+        for size in range(1, 4):
+            subsets = tuple(
+                subset
+                for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+                for subset in map(frozenset, itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size))
+            )
+            baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+            for excess_locations in itertools.product(range(len(subsets)), repeat=3):
+                weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+                for location in excess_locations:
+                    weights[subsets[location]] += 1
+                partition = weighted_cover_partition(size, weights)
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(
+                    partition,
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, baseline_mass + 3),
+                )
+
+    def test_full_support_profile_attains_the_bound(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+            for excess in (0, 1, 5, 17):
+                total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+                weights = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    weighted_cover_partition(size, weights),
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass),
+                )
+
+    def test_rank_pure_products_equal_squarefree_minima(self):
+        squarefree_indices = (
+            3,
+            5,
+            6,
+            7,
+            10,
+            15,
+            21,
+            30,
+            35,
+            42,
+            55,
+            66,
+            70,
+            78,
+            105,
+        )
+        for n in squarefree_indices:
+            with self.subTest(n=n):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    rank_pure_products(n),
+                    squarefree_minimal_generators(n),
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify the squarefree exact-fiber converse and weighted-cover sharpness."""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, Tuple
+
+from verify_deepening_delta import (
+    alpha_for_fn_divisor,
+    factorint,
+    factorint_fibonacci,
+    upper_fiber_threshold,
+)
+
+
+Subset = FrozenSet[int]
+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]
+
+
+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)
+        )
+        if frozenset().union(*cover) != vertex_set:
+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)
+
+
+def weighted_cover_partition(size: int, weights: Dict[Subset, int]) -> int:
+    """Return the weighted partition function over irredundant covers."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    if set(weights) != set(subsets) or any(weights[subset] < 1 for subset in subsets):
+        raise ValueError("weights must be positive on every nonempty subset")
+    return sum(
+        _product(weights[edge] for edge in cover)
+        for cover in minimal_covers(size)
+    )
+
+
+def _product(values: Iterable[int]) -> int:
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def sharp_mass_lower_bound(size: int, total_mass: int) -> int:
+    """Return C_k + total_mass - (2^k - 1)."""
+    baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    return len(minimal_covers(size)) + total_mass - baseline_mass
+
+
+def extremal_full_support_profile(size: int, total_mass: int) -> Dict[Subset, int]:
+    """Concentrate all mass above one on the full support."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+    weights[frozenset(range(size))] += total_mass - baseline_mass
+    return weights
+
+
+def squarefree_minimal_generators(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the squarefree elements among the verified minimal generators."""
+    result = upper_fiber_threshold(n)
+    return tuple(
+        value
+        for value in result.minimal_generators
+        if all(exponent == 1 for exponent in factorint(value).values())
+    )
+
+
+def _exact_rank_primes(n: int) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    primes_by_rank: Dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for prime, _ in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime, n)
+        primes_by_rank.setdefault(rank, []).append(prime)
+    return {
+        rank: tuple(sorted(primes))
+        for rank, primes in primes_by_rank.items()
+    }
+
+
+def rank_pure_products(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Construct the rank-pure products directly from exact-rank prime covers."""
+    n_factors = factorint(n)
+    if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in n_factors.values()):
+        raise ValueError("rank-pure converse verifier requires squarefree n")
+    coordinates = tuple(sorted(n_factors))
+    primes_by_rank = _exact_rank_primes(n)
+    products = set()
+    for cover in minimal_covers(len(coordinates)):
+        ranks = tuple(
+            _product(coordinates[index] for index in support)
+            for support in cover
+        )
+        choices = []
+        fillable = True
+        for rank in ranks:
+            primes = primes_by_rank.get(rank, tuple())
+            if not primes:
+                fillable = False
+                break
+            choices.append(primes)
+        if not fillable:
+            continue
+        for selected in itertools.product(*choices):
+            products.add(_product(selected))
+    return tuple(sorted(products))
+
+
+def run_battery(max_index: int) -> str:
+    """Run exhaustive combinatorial checks and squarefree Fibonacci comparisons."""
+    if max_index < 30:
+        raise ValueError("max_index must be at least 30")
+    profile_checks = 0
+    for size in range(1, 5):
+        baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+        for excess in range(9):
+            total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+            profile = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+            actual = weighted_cover_partition(size, profile)
+            expected = sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass)
+            if actual != expected:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"sharp profile failed for size={size}, mass={total_mass}"
+                )
+            profile_checks += 1
+
+    checked_indices = []
+    checked_elements = 0
+    for n in range(3, max_index + 1):
+        if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in factorint(n).values()):
+            continue
+        expected = squarefree_minimal_generators(n)
+        actual = rank_pure_products(n)
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"squarefree slice failed at n={n}: {actual} != {expected}"
+            )
+        checked_indices.append(n)
+        checked_elements += len(actual)
+
+    lines = [
+        "Squarefree-fiber and weighted-cover verification",
+        "=================================================",
+        "Weighted minimal-cover equality profiles: sizes 1 <= k <= 4,",
+        "  excess masses 0 <= E <= 8",
+        f"  exact equality checks = {profile_checks}",
+        f"Squarefree Fibonacci indices: 3 <= n <= {max_index}",
+        f"  indices checked = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  rank-pure/squarefree set equalities = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  squarefree minimal generators compared = {checked_elements}",
+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-index", type=int, default=210)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("artifacts/squarefree_slice_verification.txt"),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run_battery(args.max_index)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="ascii")
+    print(report, end="")
+    print(f"Saved report: {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

index 57e9e318620f502d0df011cd886f2cc3f6b143b9..8bff686c381450c84edbf29c6bf607ce96756a10

+\begin{corollary}[Canonical squarefree exact-fiber slice]
+\label{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}

+\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+ \mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}
+ =\mathcal M_n\cap\{q:\mu^2(q)=1\}
+ =\min_{\mid}\{q:\alpha(q)=n,\ \mu^2(q)=1\}.
+\end{equation}

+\end{corollary}

+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives

+has a proper divisor in $B_n$, that divisor is again squarefree.  Hence
+minimality in the squarefree part of the exact fiber is equivalent to
+membership in $\mathcal M_n$.

+belongs to $\mathcal M_n$, which proves one inclusion in the first equality.

+factorization from Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} consists only of
+prime atoms $p$.  Put $S=T_n(p)$.  Since $\alpha(p)\mid n$ and $n$ is
+squarefree,
+\[
+ \alpha(p)=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell=n_S.
+\]
+Moreover $d^-(p)=1$, so $E_n(p)=T_n(p)=S$.  The witness-cover conditions are
+therefore precisely that the distinct supports $S$ form an irredundant cover
+of $\mathcal P(n)$.  No such support lies in $\mathcal E_n$, because the
+corresponding prime $p$ itself has exact rank $n_S$.  Thus the atomic
+factorization of $m$ is one of the uniquely represented products defining
+$\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$.  This proves the reverse inclusion and the result.
+\end{proof}

+The following sharp extremal calculation separates total primitive-prime
+mass from the dispersion information retained by the cover polynomial.

+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
+$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
+\[
+ Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+
+Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\ge
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
+extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
+asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
+over all minimal covers therefore gives
+\[
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
+ =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\]
+The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
+full-support profile has weighted sum
+$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
+to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of
+$F_n$, and $a(1)=0$, so
+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
+ =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
+Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regression tests for the squarefree-fiber and sharpness verifier."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+from verify_squarefree_slice import (
+    extremal_full_support_profile,
+    minimal_covers,
+    rank_pure_products,
+    sharp_mass_lower_bound,
+    squarefree_minimal_generators,
+    weighted_cover_partition,
+)
+
+
+class SquarefreeSliceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_nonempty_subset_occurs_in_a_minimal_cover(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+            covers = minimal_covers(size)
+            for subset_size in range(1, size + 1):
+                for subset in itertools.combinations(vertex_set, subset_size):
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        any(frozenset(subset) in cover for cover in covers)
+                    )
+
+    def test_sharp_mass_bound_for_small_integer_profiles(self):
+        for size in range(1, 4):
+            subsets = tuple(
+                subset
+                for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+                for subset in map(frozenset, itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size))
+            )
+            baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+            for excess_locations in itertools.product(range(len(subsets)), repeat=3):
+                weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+                for location in excess_locations:
+                    weights[subsets[location]] += 1
+                partition = weighted_cover_partition(size, weights)
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(
+                    partition,
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, baseline_mass + 3),
+                )
+
+    def test_full_support_profile_attains_the_bound(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+            for excess in (0, 1, 5, 17):
+                total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+                weights = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    weighted_cover_partition(size, weights),
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass),
+                )
+
+    def test_rank_pure_products_equal_squarefree_minima(self):
+        squarefree_indices = (
+            3,
+            5,
+            6,
+            7,
+            10,
+            15,
+            21,
+            30,
+            35,
+            42,
+            55,
+            66,
+            70,
+            78,
+            105,
+        )
+        for n in squarefree_indices:
+            with self.subTest(n=n):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    rank_pure_products(n),
+                    squarefree_minimal_generators(n),
+                )
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify the squarefree exact-fiber converse and weighted-cover sharpness."""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, Tuple
+
+from verify_deepening_delta import (
+    alpha_for_fn_divisor,
+    factorint,
+    factorint_fibonacci,
+    upper_fiber_threshold,
+)
+
+
+Subset = FrozenSet[int]
+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]
+
+
+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)
+        )
+        if frozenset().union(*cover) != vertex_set:
+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)
+
+
+def weighted_cover_partition(size: int, weights: Dict[Subset, int]) -> int:
+    """Return the weighted partition function over irredundant covers."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    if set(weights) != set(subsets) or any(weights[subset] < 1 for subset in subsets):
+        raise ValueError("weights must be positive on every nonempty subset")
+    return sum(
+        _product(weights[edge] for edge in cover)
+        for cover in minimal_covers(size)
+    )
+
+
+def _product(values: Iterable[int]) -> int:
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def sharp_mass_lower_bound(size: int, total_mass: int) -> int:
+    """Return C_k + total_mass - (2^k - 1)."""
+    baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    return len(minimal_covers(size)) + total_mass - baseline_mass
+
+
+def extremal_full_support_profile(size: int, total_mass: int) -> Dict[Subset, int]:
+    """Concentrate all mass above one on the full support."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+    weights[frozenset(range(size))] += total_mass - baseline_mass
+    return weights
+
+
+def squarefree_minimal_generators(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the squarefree elements among the verified minimal generators."""
+    result = upper_fiber_threshold(n)
+    return tuple(
+        value
+        for value in result.minimal_generators
+        if all(exponent == 1 for exponent in factorint(value).values())
+    )
+
+
+def _exact_rank_primes(n: int) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    primes_by_rank: Dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for prime, _ in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime, n)
+        primes_by_rank.setdefault(rank, []).append(prime)
+    return {
+        rank: tuple(sorted(primes))
+        for rank, primes in primes_by_rank.items()
+    }
+
+
+def rank_pure_products(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Construct the rank-pure products directly from exact-rank prime covers."""
+    n_factors = factorint(n)
+    if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in n_factors.values()):
+        raise ValueError("rank-pure converse verifier requires squarefree n")
+    coordinates = tuple(sorted(n_factors))
+    primes_by_rank = _exact_rank_primes(n)
+    products = set()
+    for cover in minimal_covers(len(coordinates)):
+        ranks = tuple(
+            _product(coordinates[index] for index in support)
+            for support in cover
+        )
+        choices = []
+        fillable = True
+        for rank in ranks:
+            primes = primes_by_rank.get(rank, tuple())
+            if not primes:
+                fillable = False
+                break
+            choices.append(primes)
+        if not fillable:
+            continue
+        for selected in itertools.product(*choices):
+            products.add(_product(selected))
+    return tuple(sorted(products))
+
+
+def run_battery(max_index: int) -> str:
+    """Run exhaustive combinatorial checks and squarefree Fibonacci comparisons."""
+    if max_index < 30:
+        raise ValueError("max_index must be at least 30")
+    profile_checks = 0
+    for size in range(1, 5):
+        baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+        for excess in range(9):
+            total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+            profile = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+            actual = weighted_cover_partition(size, profile)
+            expected = sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass)
+            if actual != expected:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"sharp profile failed for size={size}, mass={total_mass}"
+                )
+            profile_checks += 1
+
+    checked_indices = []
+    checked_elements = 0
+    for n in range(3, max_index + 1):
+        if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in factorint(n).values()):
+            continue
+        expected = squarefree_minimal_generators(n)
+        actual = rank_pure_products(n)
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"squarefree slice failed at n={n}: {actual} != {expected}"
+            )
+        checked_indices.append(n)
+        checked_elements += len(actual)
+
+    lines = [
+        "Squarefree-fiber and weighted-cover verification",
+        "=================================================",
+        "Weighted minimal-cover equality profiles: sizes 1 <= k <= 4,",
+        "  excess masses 0 <= E <= 8",
+        f"  exact equality checks = {profile_checks}",
+        f"Squarefree Fibonacci indices: 3 <= n <= {max_index}",
+        f"  indices checked = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  rank-pure/squarefree set equalities = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  squarefree minimal generators compared = {checked_elements}",
+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-index", type=int, default=210)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("artifacts/squarefree_slice_verification.txt"),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run_battery(args.max_index)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="ascii")
+    print(report, end="")
+    print(f"Saved report: {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+The rank-pure sector has a canonical description on squarefree indices.  In
+particular, it is not then an auxiliary class defined only through the cover
+construction.
+
+\begin{corollary}[Canonical squarefree exact-fiber slice]
+\label{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+Let $n\ge3$ be squarefree.  Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:canonical-squarefree-slice}
+ \mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}
+ =\mathcal M_n\cap\{q:\mu^2(q)=1\}
+ =\min_{\mid}\{q:\alpha(q)=n,\ \mu^2(q)=1\}.
+\end{equation}
+Thus the weighted sum in
+\eqref{eq:rank-pure-weighted-sector} counts exactly the divisibility-minimal
+squarefree elements of the standard exact fiber $\alpha^{-1}(n)$.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:rank-basics} gives
+$B_n=\{q:\alpha(q)=n\}=\alpha^{-1}(n)$.  If a squarefree member of $B_n$
+has a proper divisor in $B_n$, that divisor is again squarefree.  Hence
+minimality in the squarefree part of the exact fiber is equivalent to
+membership in $\mathcal M_n$.
+
+Every element of $\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$ is a product of distinct primes and
+belongs to $\mathcal M_n$, which proves one inclusion in the first equality.
+Conversely, let $m\in\mathcal M_n$ be squarefree.  Its unique atomic
+factorization from Theorem~\ref{thm:witness-classification} consists only of
+prime atoms $p$.  Put $S=T_n(p)$.  Since $\alpha(p)\mid n$ and $n$ is
+squarefree,
+\[
+ \alpha(p)=\prod_{\ell\in S}\ell=n_S.
+\]
+Moreover $d^-(p)=1$, so $E_n(p)=T_n(p)=S$.  The witness-cover conditions are
+therefore precisely that the distinct supports $S$ form an irredundant cover
+of $\mathcal P(n)$.  No such support lies in $\mathcal E_n$, because the
+corresponding prime $p$ itself has exact rank $n_S$.  Thus the atomic
+factorization of $m$ is one of the uniquely represented products defining
+$\mathcal R_n^{\rm rp}$.  This proves the reverse inclusion and the result.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{cor:odd-rank-pure-universality}
 Let $n\ge3$ be odd and put $k=\omega(n)$. Then $\mathcal E_n=\varnothing$.
 After fixing one prime $\pi_S\in\Pi_\alpha(n_S)$ for every nonempty
@@ -191,4 +232,72 @@

 \end{proof}
+
+The following sharp extremal calculation separates total primitive-prime
+mass from the dispersion information retained by the cover polynomial.
+
+\begin{proposition}[Sharp cumulative-data obstruction]
+\label{prop:sharp-cumulative-data-obstruction}
+Let $V$ be a labelled $k$-set, $k\ge1$, and assign a real weight
+$w_S\ge1$ to every nonempty $S\subseteq V$.  Put
+\[
+ Z_V(w):=\sum_{\mathcal C\in\operatorname{MinCov}(V)}
+              \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}w_S,
+ \qquad A:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}w_S.
+\]
+Then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\end{equation}
+This is best possible for every $A\ge2^k-1$: equality is attained by
+\[
+ w_V=A-(2^k-2),\qquad w_S=1\quad(S\ne V).
+\]
+
+Consequently, if $n\ge3$ is odd and squarefree and $k=\omega(n)$, then
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-rank-pure-bound}
+ \#\{m\in\mathcal M_n:\mu^2(m)=1\}
+ \ge C_k+\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1),
+\end{equation}
+and
+\begin{equation}\label{eq:squarefree-cumulative-weighted-excess}
+ \mathcal W(n)\ge
+ 1+\frac{\omega(F_n)-(2^k-1)}{C_k}.
+\end{equation}
+Among all positive weight profiles with the same total
+$\sum_{d\mid n,\ d>1}a(d)=\omega(F_n)$, this conclusion is exact.  The
+extremizing profile is an abstract information-theoretic model; it is not
+asserted to be realized by Fibonacci exact-rank primes.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Write $w_S=1+x_S$ with $x_S\ge0$.  For every minimal cover $\mathcal C$,
+\[
+ \prod_{S\in\mathcal C}(1+x_S)
+ \ge1+\sum_{S\in\mathcal C}x_S.
+\]
+Every nonempty $S\subseteq V$ occurs in a minimal cover: use $\{V\}$ when
+$S=V$, and otherwise use
+$\{S\}\cup\{\{v\}:v\in V\setminus S\}$.  Summing the preceding inequality
+over all minimal covers therefore gives
+\[
+ Z_V(w)\ge C_k+\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq V}x_S
+ =C_k+A-(2^k-1).
+\]
+The only minimal cover containing $V$ is $\{V\}$.  Hence the displayed
+full-support profile has weighted sum
+$C_k-1+w_V=C_k+A-(2^k-1)$, proving sharpness.
+
+For odd squarefree $n$, the nonempty subsets of $\mathcal P(n)$ correspond
+to the divisors $d>1$ of $n$.  Exact ranks partition the prime divisors of
+$F_n$, and $a(1)=0$, so
+\[
+ \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\mathcal P(n)}a(n_S)
+ =\sum_{d\mid n}a(d)=\omega(F_n).
+\]
+Every weight is positive by exact-rank prime existence.  Apply
+\eqref{eq:sharp-total-mass-cover-bound}, then use
+Corollary~\ref{cor:canonical-squarefree-slice} and
+\eqref{eq:weighted-cover-excess}.
+\end{proof}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regression tests for the squarefree-fiber and sharpness verifier."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+from verify_squarefree_slice import (
+    extremal_full_support_profile,
+    minimal_covers,
+    rank_pure_products,
+    sharp_mass_lower_bound,
+    squarefree_minimal_generators,
+    weighted_cover_partition,
+)
+
+
+class SquarefreeSliceTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_nonempty_subset_occurs_in_a_minimal_cover(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+            covers = minimal_covers(size)
+            for subset_size in range(1, size + 1):
+                for subset in itertools.combinations(vertex_set, subset_size):
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        any(frozenset(subset) in cover for cover in covers)
+                    )
+
+    def test_sharp_mass_bound_for_small_integer_profiles(self):
+        for size in range(1, 4):
+            subsets = tuple(
+                subset
+                for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+                for subset in map(frozenset, itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size))
+            )
+            baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+            for excess_locations in itertools.product(range(len(subsets)), repeat=3):
+                weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+                for location in excess_locations:
+                    weights[subsets[location]] += 1
+                partition = weighted_cover_partition(size, weights)
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(
+                    partition,
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, baseline_mass + 3),
+                )
+
+    def test_full_support_profile_attains_the_bound(self):
+        for size in range(1, 5):
+            baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+            for excess in (0, 1, 5, 17):
+                total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+                weights = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    weighted_cover_partition(size, weights),
+                    sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass),
+                )
+
+    def test_rank_pure_products_equal_squarefree_minima(self):
+        squarefree_indices = (
+            3,
+            5,
+            6,
+            7,
+            10,
+            15,
+            21,
+            30,
+            35,
+            42,
+            55,
+            66,
+            70,
+            78,
+            105,
+        )
+        for n in squarefree_indices:
+            with self.subTest(n=n):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    rank_pure_products(n),
+                    squarefree_minimal_generators(n),
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify the squarefree exact-fiber converse and weighted-cover sharpness."""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Dict, FrozenSet, Iterable, Tuple
+
+from verify_deepening_delta import (
+    alpha_for_fn_divisor,
+    factorint,
+    factorint_fibonacci,
+    upper_fiber_threshold,
+)
+
+
+Subset = FrozenSet[int]
+Cover = FrozenSet[Subset]
+
+
+def _nonempty_subsets(size: int) -> Tuple[Subset, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        frozenset(subset)
+        for subset_size in range(1, size + 1)
+        for subset in itertools.combinations(range(size), subset_size)
+    )
+
+
+def minimal_covers(size: int) -> Tuple[Cover, ...]:
+    """Enumerate irredundant covers of a labelled set of the given size."""
+    if size < 1:
+        raise ValueError("size must be positive")
+    vertex_set = frozenset(range(size))
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    covers = []
+    for mask in range(1, 1 << len(subsets)):
+        cover = frozenset(
+            subsets[index]
+            for index in range(len(subsets))
+            if mask & (1 << index)
+        )
+        if frozenset().union(*cover) != vertex_set:
+            continue
+        if all(
+            edge - frozenset().union(*(cover - {edge}))
+            for edge in cover
+        ):
+            covers.append(cover)
+    return tuple(covers)
+
+
+def weighted_cover_partition(size: int, weights: Dict[Subset, int]) -> int:
+    """Return the weighted partition function over irredundant covers."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    if set(weights) != set(subsets) or any(weights[subset] < 1 for subset in subsets):
+        raise ValueError("weights must be positive on every nonempty subset")
+    return sum(
+        _product(weights[edge] for edge in cover)
+        for cover in minimal_covers(size)
+    )
+
+
+def _product(values: Iterable[int]) -> int:
+    result = 1
+    for value in values:
+        result *= value
+    return result
+
+
+def sharp_mass_lower_bound(size: int, total_mass: int) -> int:
+    """Return C_k + total_mass - (2^k - 1)."""
+    baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    return len(minimal_covers(size)) + total_mass - baseline_mass
+
+
+def extremal_full_support_profile(size: int, total_mass: int) -> Dict[Subset, int]:
+    """Concentrate all mass above one on the full support."""
+    subsets = _nonempty_subsets(size)
+    baseline_mass = len(subsets)
+    if total_mass < baseline_mass:
+        raise ValueError("positive weights require total_mass >= 2^size - 1")
+    weights = {subset: 1 for subset in subsets}
+    weights[frozenset(range(size))] += total_mass - baseline_mass
+    return weights
+
+
+def squarefree_minimal_generators(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Return the squarefree elements among the verified minimal generators."""
+    result = upper_fiber_threshold(n)
+    return tuple(
+        value
+        for value in result.minimal_generators
+        if all(exponent == 1 for exponent in factorint(value).values())
+    )
+
+
+def _exact_rank_primes(n: int) -> Dict[int, Tuple[int, ...]]:
+    primes_by_rank: Dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for prime, _ in factorint_fibonacci(n):
+        rank = alpha_for_fn_divisor(prime, n)
+        primes_by_rank.setdefault(rank, []).append(prime)
+    return {
+        rank: tuple(sorted(primes))
+        for rank, primes in primes_by_rank.items()
+    }
+
+
+def rank_pure_products(n: int) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
+    """Construct the rank-pure products directly from exact-rank prime covers."""
+    n_factors = factorint(n)
+    if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in n_factors.values()):
+        raise ValueError("rank-pure converse verifier requires squarefree n")
+    coordinates = tuple(sorted(n_factors))
+    primes_by_rank = _exact_rank_primes(n)
+    products = set()
+    for cover in minimal_covers(len(coordinates)):
+        ranks = tuple(
+            _product(coordinates[index] for index in support)
+            for support in cover
+        )
+        choices = []
+        fillable = True
+        for rank in ranks:
+            primes = primes_by_rank.get(rank, tuple())
+            if not primes:
+                fillable = False
+                break
+            choices.append(primes)
+        if not fillable:
+            continue
+        for selected in itertools.product(*choices):
+            products.add(_product(selected))
+    return tuple(sorted(products))
+
+
+def run_battery(max_index: int) -> str:
+    """Run exhaustive combinatorial checks and squarefree Fibonacci comparisons."""
+    if max_index < 30:
+        raise ValueError("max_index must be at least 30")
+    profile_checks = 0
+    for size in range(1, 5):
+        baseline_mass = 2**size - 1
+        for excess in range(9):
+            total_mass = baseline_mass + excess
+            profile = extremal_full_support_profile(size, total_mass)
+            actual = weighted_cover_partition(size, profile)
+            expected = sharp_mass_lower_bound(size, total_mass)
+            if actual != expected:
+                raise AssertionError(
+                    f"sharp profile failed for size={size}, mass={total_mass}"
+                )
+            profile_checks += 1
+
+    checked_indices = []
+    checked_elements = 0
+    for n in range(3, max_index + 1):
+        if any(exponent != 1 for exponent in factorint(n).values()):
+            continue
+        expected = squarefree_minimal_generators(n)
+        actual = rank_pure_products(n)
+        if actual != expected:
+            raise AssertionError(
+                f"squarefree slice failed at n={n}: {actual} != {expected}"
+            )
+        checked_indices.append(n)
+        checked_elements += len(actual)
+
+    lines = [
+        "Squarefree-fiber and weighted-cover verification",
+        "=================================================",
+        "Weighted minimal-cover equality profiles: sizes 1 <= k <= 4,",
+        "  excess masses 0 <= E <= 8",
+        f"  exact equality checks = {profile_checks}",
+        f"Squarefree Fibonacci indices: 3 <= n <= {max_index}",
+        f"  indices checked = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  rank-pure/squarefree set equalities = {len(checked_indices)}",
+        f"  squarefree minimal generators compared = {checked_elements}",
+        "RESULT: PASS (0 failures / 0 counterexamples)",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-index", type=int, default=210)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path("artifacts/squarefree_slice_verification.txt"),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    report = run_battery(args.max_index)
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(report, encoding="ascii")
+    print(report, end="")
+    print(f"Saved report: {args.output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
